done_when: Close writes the proof list from the tests it ran and their results, and the worker only names which Done-when item each test proves, so a proof list never names a test that did not run

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 1
Raise: Not done. When a worker writes a normal Markdown code span such as `tests/test_greeting.py::test_returning`, TEST_NAME consumes the closing backtick as part of the node ID. The source check then fails and Close publishes `not run` for a test that ran. The command-level proof uses only unwrapped node IDs. This leaves the Done-when requirement unmet for a common proof-list format.
findings.title: Not done: Close cannot match Markdown-wrapped pytest node IDs

findings.body:
Gain 2, Work 2, Harm 1
Raise: Functional. For one test whose call passes but fixture teardown fails, the new hook writes both `passed` and `error` for the same node ID (fasttest.py:363-374). This counter treats those phase reports as separate cases, so Close publishes `1 passed, 1 error` for one errored test. The named command test covers an assertion failure, leaving this incorrect result and case count undetected.
findings.title: Close counts a failed teardown as a second test case

stop.reason: Coordinator (Harm 2, reversible): one last round on the two cases workers hit every day — names wrapped in Markdown code marks match like plain names, and each test counts once with a failed teardown counted as that test's failure. Anything further in review.py is accepted as a follow-up.

why: Workers write proof lists by hand, and about one review round in five is a gate on a missing or wrong test name in that list
